articles.title: Best Vocal Mics For Producers Recording In Untreated Rooms Based On My Tests
articles.excerpt: Home / Gear Recording vocals in an untreated room changes what I want from a microphone. Extra detail sounds appealing on paper, yet bedroom walls, computer fans, hard floors, and traffic can become far easier to hear once compression lifts the lower-level information in the take. The wrong microphone can leave you spending half the mix trying to reduce a room sound that was recorded from the start. That is why I pay close attention to pickup pattern, rear rejection, and working distance when reviewing microphones in my home studio. A condenser can capture an impressive amount of vocal detail from the right position, though it can also pick up reflections that a directional microphone places much farther behind the singer. articles.excerpt: Consider Arca a cyborg, a performance artist more so than a producer. For the Venezuelan visionary, the sonic and somatic are inseparable, her music an extension of her physical form, a document of becoming — each project another transmutation from one body into the next. On paper, it sounds like the most natural thing in the room. Instead of triggering samples, the synth models the behavior of strings, tubes, membranes, plates, bells, drumheads, and other resonant bodies. Ozora_A.excerpt: Hungary’s Ozora Festival was cut short this past weekend following the death of two attendees in separate incidents on site. The festival, which is one of the largest psychedelic trance music events in Europe, kicked off on Friday, 24th July, and was supposed to conclude on Tuesday 4th August. However, festival organisers confirmed on Sunday (2nd) that the music programme would be suspended from midnight following the tragic fatalities. On Saturday, a 39-year-old Hungarian woman passed away after a sudden cardiac arrest at the site in Dadpuszta, Hungary. According to festival organisers, she received treatment within minutes, but emergency medical services were unable to revive her. Better.title: VLAD – Datso
Better.excerpt: VLAD - Datso - By The Wavs You are here: Home / Music / House / Tech House / VLAD – Datso on on X Pin this A track called VLAD sets you up for something with fangs. Datso hands you the opposite: loose, grinning, a tech house groove that is in a good mood before the first bar even lands. VLAD anchors his Sans Stress EP, and it earns the spot. The bassline carries the whole thing, a round low end bouncing on the off-beat without ever pushing. A vocal gets chopped to a couple of syllables and dropped in just often enough to keep your head moving. Datso runs the percussion tight and the top end dry, and once the groove locks in after the first break it keeps that exact pace to the end. matches.title: Two attendees die at Hungary's Ozora Festival, event ends early
matches.excerpt: Hungary’s Ozora Festival was cut short this past weekend following the death of two attendees in separate incidents on site. The festival, which is one of the largest psychedelic trance music events in Europe, kicked off on Friday, 24th July, and was supposed to conclude on Tuesday 4th August. However, festival organisers confirmed on Sunday (2nd) that the music programme would be suspended from midnight following the tragic fatalities. On Saturday, a 39-year-old Hungarian woman passed away after a sudden cardiac arrest at the site in Dadpuszta, Hungary. According to festival organisers, she received treatment within minutes, but emergency medical services were unable to revive her.
